51.0.s.en: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

51.0.0.en: 1 Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD: look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. 2 Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him. 3 For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody. 4 Hearken unto me, my people; and give ear unto me, O my nation: for a law shall proceed from me, and I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people. 5 My righteousness is near; my salvation is gone forth, and mine arms shall judge the people; the isles shall wait upon me, and on mine arm shall they trust. 6 Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished. 7 Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings. 8 For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation. 9 Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? 10 Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over? 11 Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away. 12 I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass; 13 And forgettest the LORD thy maker, that hath stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and hast feared continually every day because of the fury of the oppressor, as if he were ready to destroy? and where is the fury of the oppressor? 14 The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail. 15 But I am the LORD thy God, that divided the sea, whose waves roared: The LORD of hosts is his name. 16 And I have put my words in thy mouth, and I have covered thee in the shadow of mine hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and say unto Zion, Thou art my people.

51.0.1.en: In this call the word “hearken” or “give ear” is repeated three times [1, 4, 7]. If the “Word of God,” who is the Creator, the Judge and the Lawgiver, heard and obeyed, then all the more should His people be marked by a spirit of obedience... It is as though we cannot enter into the life of the Gospel and enjoy the free salvation unless we hear and give ear, that the Lord may work in us.

51.0.2.en: What is the content of the call?

51.0.3.en: a. The repetition of the word “hearken” means that the call is at its core an exhortation to obedience, the obedience of faith, full of trust in God and love.

51.0.4.en: * [Obedience makes friends of God.] He says: “If ye love me, keep my commandments” (Jn 14:15); He did not say “work miracles,” but what did He say? “Keep my commandments.”

51.0.5.en: Again: “Ye are my friends” (Jn 15:14) not when you cast out demons but “if ye do whatsoever I command you”... Let us strive to become friends of God and not remain His enemies.

51.0.6.en: St. John Chrysostom b. “Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD” [1]. Through obedience, hearing is turned into practical conduct, that is, following righteousness or walking in the way of God's righteousness, and the goal of this is seeking the Lord, meeting Him and being united with Him. This is our faith, and this is our Christianity: hearing, obedience, life, union with the Lord!

51.0.7.en: c. Imitating the faith of Abraham: “Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him” [1-2].

51.0.8.en: It is as though He says to them: if you find the call difficult, saying, how can we hear the voice of the Lord and follow His righteousness and seek Him in our life? Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you. Abraham came from a pagan family; indeed the whole world at that time had turned away from the knowledge of God, so Abraham came as though from hard rock and from clay in the hole of a pit. He heard from his parents no word of comfort; no divine law had been delivered, and no priest or prophet supported him; yet when I called him he responded. He was alone in his faith, so I blessed him and increased him... and my people came from his seed!

51.0.9.en: Truly, if we admit that Adam was created from dust, and that we have been formed from rock, with no spiritual sense, and have wallowed as in the mire of the pit, let us not despair, for our father Abraham was also of the seed of Adam, and he accepted the call and obeyed and received the divine promises in his seed.

51.0.10.en: Abraham was an old man and Sarah his wife was barren; her womb was like lifeless rock, unable to bear children, yet God raised up children to Abraham from stones.

51.0.11.en: * God is able to bring forth men from stones... For the child conceived in a petrified womb is like one born of stones...

51.0.12.en: Now in this prophecy [1-2] you see that He shows them that from the beginning He raised up a father in a miraculous way, as though from stones, and what happened before can be fulfilled now (Mt 3:5).

51.0.13.en: St. John Chrysostom * God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham (Mt 3:9). He refers here to the Gentiles, for they are stones because of the hardness of their hearts. Let us read: “And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh” (Ezek 36:26). For stone is an image of hardness, and flesh a symbol of gentleness. He wanted to show the power of God, who is able to create out of hard stones a believing people.

51.1.0.en: St. Jerome d. A call of consolation, for God turns her ruins and deserts into a garden of the Lord, or a paradise. This is God's work in His Church: He gives the fruits of His Holy Spirit to His people, so that all become a kingdom bearing fruit in the Spirit. “For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD” [3].

51.1.1.en: The Book of Isaiah often speaks of God's work of salvation as the establishing of the fruitful Kingdom of God, and the turning of the wilderness into a spiritual orchard (Isa 32:5), in which truth dwells (Isa 32:6), which rejoices and exults in God who dwells in it (Isa 35:1), and so on... He who makes of it a paradise and a heaven.

51.1.2.en: St. John Chrysostom looked upon the Church, especially when she celebrates the liturgy of the Eucharist (the Divine Liturgy), as heaven, saying: [She is higher than heaven and wider than the whole world. He speaks in the person of the Lord Christ, saying:

51.1.3.en: “I planted you in paradise, and Satan drove you out!

51.1.4.en: Behold, I plant you in Myself!

51.1.5.en: I support you, so that Satan no longer has the power to approach you.

51.1.6.en: I do not lift you up to heaven, but to here, where the Lord of heaven is.

51.1.7.en: I carry you within Me, I, the Lord of heaven!”].

51.1.8.en: St. Clement of Alexandria says: [The earthly Church is the icon of the heavenly Church; therefore we pray that the will of God be done on earth as it is in heaven. And he says: [If you enroll yourself as one of the members of the people of God, heaven becomes your city and God your lawgiver.]

51.1.9.en: e. A call to joy and gladness: “Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody” [3]. This line is clear throughout the book, being the book of salvation, which proclaims the rise of the Kingdom of inward joy and of unceasing singing and praise.

51.1.10.en: When St. John Cassian visited Egypt, he was amazed to find its deserts and villages, from Alexandria to Aswan, filled with monks, from whom nothing was heard but the sound of unceasing praise, so that he thought himself to be in heaven, asking: Are these earthly angels or heavenly men?!

51.1.11.en: This is the mark of the true Church: an inward joy that never ceases!

51.1.12.en: This joy is reflected in the whole life of the Church, and Madame Butcher observed that in the poor ancient churches of Egypt there was not one icon bearing the picture of a martyr being tortured or in pain, nor a picture of hell and its torments; rather, every icon radiates a spirit of joy and hope, so that even the martyrs you see rejoicing, looking toward heaven, gazing at the crown of their glory.

51.1.13.en: Joy is reflected in worship: on almost every day the Church celebrates a feast of the Lord, or a feast of one of the prophets, apostles, heavenly beings, martyrs, and so on... It is as though the Church creates an atmosphere of spiritual joy amid the troubles of this life, so that her children experience the consolations of the Holy Spirit and His heavenly joy; and the believer lives sharing with the heavenly beings their liturgies and their quiet, joyful exultations without interruption.

51.1.14.en: One of the prominent signs of joy in the Church is that the Holy Bible, especially the Gospels, is not read during the liturgies but chanted with a melody that fills the soul with consolation. Mr. Lieder, the well-known English writer, testified at the beginning of the nineteenth century, on his visit to Egypt, that the mere hearing of the Gospel during the Divine Liturgy in the Coptic Church has an effect on the soul.

51.2.0.en: f. A call to preaching, for whoever enjoys the joy of salvation cannot remain silent in bearing witness to the life of the Gospel, but carries the law of the Lord and His Gospel as “a light of the people” [4], assuring all that life in Christ is neither far off nor impossible, for the righteousness of Christ is near to every heart [5], and His arms are stretched out in love on the Cross to the peoples, as the hope of all [5].

51.2.1.en: Preaching, or bearing witness to the saving work of Christ, belongs to the very core of every Christian's life and is not the work of the priest alone; therefore St. John Chrysostom says:

51.2.2.en: [Nothing is so worthless as a Christian who does not care about the salvation of others.

51.2.3.en: Do not say, I am poor, for the widow's two mites put you to shame. And Peter also said: “Silver and gold have I none,” and Paul was so poor that he often suffered hunger.

51.2.4.en: Do not plead your harsh circumstances, for they too were in harsh circumstances.

51.2.5.en: Do not plead your ignorance, for they were unlearned.

51.2.6.en: Perhaps you are a runaway slave; Onesimus was also this!

51.2.7.en: You may be sick; Timothy was so!

51.2.8.en: Everyone is able to help his brother, even if only by good will, if he has not the ability to do anything...

51.2.9.en: Do not say that you cannot influence others, for as long as you are a Christian it is impossible that you should not be influential... for this is the very essence of the Christian.

51.2.10.en: If you say that you are a Christian and cannot do anything for others, there is a contradiction in your saying this, like saying that the sun cannot give light.]

51.3.0.en: g. A call to an eternal salvation that goes beyond heaven and earth: “Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished” [6].

51.3.1.en: The passing away of the heavens and the earth while salvation remains for ever signifies the crucifixion of the old man so as to enjoy the new man who is after the image of his Creator. The old heavens and the old earth must pass away in us that we may enjoy the new heavens and the new earth, whose inhabitants do not die like gnats, but in which the eternal righteousness of the Lord dwells.

51.3.2.en: If the heavens signify the soul and the earth the body, then the vanishing of the heavens and the wearing out of the earth mean the destruction of the works of the old man, for the soul as for the body, for the sanctification of our souls and our bodies, as we are the new creation renewed every day by the work of the Holy Spirit of God.

51.3.3.en: As for his saying “and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner” [6], it signifies the weakness of the works of the old man: they die like gnats! But the works of the new man are the righteousness of Christ which is not abolished, or the love which never fails.

51.4.0.en: h. A serious and courageous call not to be troubled before the opposition of men: “Fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings. For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation” [7-8].

51.4.1.en: Whoever lifts his gaze to the eternal Savior does not fear the actions of men and their opposition, for they come to nothing and end, while our salvation remains eternal.

51.4.2.en: The living spiritual man looks to his old man, whom he put off in the waters of Baptism like a garment that has worn out, and like a gnat that died in weakness; as for the reproaches of men and their revilings, they are like a garment eaten by the moth and like wool eaten by the worm! They are worn-out temporal things that will not last long; we bear them without being troubled, for in this we share with our Savior, who bore reproaches and insults gladly for our sake. Meet evil with love, bearing the weaknesses of the wicked.

51.4.3.en: * Do not put out fire with another fire, but with water.

51.4.4.en: * Nothing restrains evildoers from their evil like the injured person's meeting with gentleness the harm that befalls him.

51.5.0.en: St. John Chrysostom i. A call to enjoy the risen life that overcomes death and crushes the murderous dragon. “Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon?” [9].

51.5.1.en: The Church is the “arm of the LORD” who puts on the strength of His resurrection and awakes as from the sleep of death. Let the whole Church rise, whether those who came from a Jewish origin or a Gentile one; therefore He repeats the word “awake” twice.

51.5.2.en: God, the Giver of victory, formerly gave her strength and she overcame Egypt (the poetic name Rahab, as we saw earlier) when He rescued her from the hand of Pharaoh, who drowned in the waters of the Red Sea like a pierced dragon unable to live. It is the Lord Himself who gives His Church in the New Testament the power of His resurrection, not to overcome Pharaoh but the powers of darkness, and not to find a way for herself in the midst of the sea but to pass over into heaven itself.

51.5.3.en: * Now that death has been abolished (by the resurrection of the Lord Christ), and the kingdom of Satan has been demolished, all are filled with joy and happiness.

51.5.4.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic j. A call to enjoy God Himself as the Comforter: “I, even I, am he that comforteth you” (Isa 59:12), without seeking human consolations or fearing the troubling by men, for their life is but like grass (Isa 59:12).

51.6.0.en: In our enjoyment of God's consolations we must not fear man, for he is transient, and his troubling is transient too; if we are disturbed by him we live in dread every day [14], though there is nothing to deserve it.

51.6.1.en: Despair came upon the captives and they thought that they would die in captivity, but God assured them: “The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit (in captivity), nor that his bread should fail” [14]. It is fitting for them to wait for God's promise and never despair. If the kingdom of Babylon has drowned them like the sea, the Savior, the LORD of hosts, is able to trouble Babylon: “But I am the LORD thy God, that divided the sea, whose waves roared: The LORD of hosts is his name” (Isa 49:15).

51.7.s.en: 2. The mystery of the fall of Jerusalem:

51.7.0.en: 17 Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out. 18 There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she hath brought forth; neither is there any that taketh her by the hand of all the sons that she hath brought up. 19 These two things are come unto thee; who shall be sorry for thee? desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword: by whom shall I comfort thee? 20 Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of thy God.

51.7.1.en: After presenting this joyful call to enjoy the new life in the Lord, He wished to make plain the mystery of Jerusalem's captivity, so that she might realize her weaknesses and rise from her falls. Therefore He began by saying: “Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem” [17]. What He reveals of the weaknesses that struck her is not meant to expose her to shame, but is an uncovering of the wounds in order to treat them, and an explanation of the mystery of the fall so that she may rise and stand. Her weaknesses are summed up in her drinking “at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling” [17].

51.7.2.en: It was the custom to give those condemned to death a cup of strong wine so that they would stagger before the sentence was carried out; so Jerusalem drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of His fury over her sins, that she might realize that she had fallen under punishment, not by her captivity to Babylon but by her captivity under the sentence of death, because her sins had taken her captive and made her lose her consciousness.

51.8.0.en: She drank of her own will from the cup of disobedience and staggered, and she found none among them to take her by the hand; she became like a mother whom her children despise without being ashamed. Those who sorrow over her state became “desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword” [19].

51.9.0.en: 21 Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine: 22 Thus saith thy Lord the LORD, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: 23 But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.

51.9.1.en: With every uncovering of weakness or evil, the Lord opens the door of hope for salvation. Therefore, after He revealed to her the mystery of her fall, not in the Babylonian captivity but in the captivity of sin, and her drinking of the cup of God's wrath so as to stagger, He went on to assure her that He pardons her, handing the cup to her oppressors, who said to her soul: “Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.” It was the custom for the conquerors to walk with their feet on the necks of the defeated. Therefore the conquerors commanded her to throw herself on the ground so that the enemy might walk on her back like a narrow street in which they pass. She lived in humiliation because she left God and disobeyed Him... Now He forgives her and sets her free!
